item.title: Los Angeles Prosecutor to Oversee Inquiry Into Search of Trump’s Mar-a-Lago Residence
item.description: The appointment of Bill Essayli to run a key aspect of the so-called grand conspiracy case was the latest shake-up in a central part of President Trump’s retribution campaign.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer
item.category: Federal Criminal Case Against Trump (Documents Case)
item.media:credit: David Crane/Los Angeles Daily News, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Bill Essayli will focus narrowly on the question of whether agents and prosecutors broke the law four years ago when they searched Mar-a-Lago.

item.title: A Paramedic Rushed to a Fatal Accident. The Dead Man Was Her Son.
item.description: The paramedic in rural Utah realized a man pinned under a car was her son after she began treating him, the authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Karla Adam
item.media:credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
item.media:description: A paramedic in Utah responded to a fatal accident involving her own son, a father of two young children.

item.title: In Bending to Trump, Law Firm Did $11.8 Million of Free Work for Administration
item.description: The firm Kirkland & Ellis has quietly disclosed that as part of the deal it reached with the Trump administration, it has done about 6,491 hours of free work.
item.dc:creator: Michael S. Schmidt
item.media:description: Boris Epshteyn, one of the president’s personal lawyers, helped to negotiate a deal with Kirkland & Ellis to complete free work for the Trump administration.

item.title: Boston’s Beloved Citgo Sign Returns After Rebuild, 30 Feet Higher
item.description: The beloved Citgo sign will be lit again on Thursday night after it was rebuilt and moved 120 feet to the east, its latest incarnation in a city transformed by development.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Russell
item.media:description: The Citgo sign in Boston, gleaming over Kenmore Square in September 2025, before it went dark and was rebuilt

item.title: Three MAGA Women Who Defined an Era in Congress Are Exiting
item.description: Representatives Marjorie Taylor Greene, Lauren Boebert and Nancy Mace embodied a combative, attention-seeking brand of politics that defined the Republican Congress.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.media:credit: Tom Brenner for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representatives Lauren Boebert and Marjorie Taylor Greene speak to Rep. Scott Perry following a meeting on Capitol Hill in 2022.

item.title: Anthropic Employees Work Hard, but Don’t Expect Them to Play Hard
item.description: San Francisco isn’t preparing for an Anthropic shopping spree after employees gain newfound wealth from the company’s initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Heather Knight and Emmy Martin
item.media:description: Hundreds more San Franciscans will be able to call themselves multimillionaires — and a handful will even become multibillionaires.

item.title: ‘GTA Flu’ Has Schools and Jobs Bracing for Sick Days
item.description: The highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to prompt a wave of students and employees to stay home on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Mack Liederman and Ishani Desai
item.media:description: Grand Theft Auto VI is rolling out worldwide on Thursday.

item.title: With Alaska’s Senate Vote Counted, What Comes Next in the Last Frontier?
item.description: The race is scheduled to be certified next week, but the Justice Department is investigating after Republicans lodged cheating allegations against the eventual winner, Mary Peltola.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning
item.media:credit: Christopher Miller for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Alaska Senate race did not require the state’s ranked-choice voting procedure, but the House race did.

item.title: Alaska Republican Narrowly Defeats Independent House Candidate
item.description: Representative Nick Begich III overcame an independent challenger in a year in which Democrats made historic gains but third-party candidates had little success.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:description: Representative Nick Begich of Alaska at a watch party in Anchorage on Election Day.

item.title: Ericka Lomick’s Texas House Win Faces Challenge in State Supreme Court
item.description: The Texas electoral wave carried one Democrat to victory even after she had suspended her campaign. Republicans want her declared ineligible.
item.dc:creator: J. David Goodman
item.media:description: Voters lined up to cast their ballots on Election Day in Fort Worth, Texas.

item.title: Obama Tells Incoming House Democrats to Keep Up Outreach in Red Areas
item.description: The former president told the newly elected lawmakers that the country was going through a moment of “generational change.” He also praised Representative Hakeem Jeffries, the likely next speaker.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former President Barack Obama at a rally in Michigan in October. He campaigned for Democratic candidates in several states during the midterm elections.

item.description: Lawmakers and cyberdefense experts said diminished staffing at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and National Security Council could be hobbling the administration’s response.

item.title: Trump Weighs New Strikes on Iran as Israel Presses for Action, Officials Say
item.description: Warnings that Iran is rebuilding its missile stockpile and advancing biological and chemical programs have divided the Trump administration.
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes, Eric Schmitt, Maggie Haberman, Jonathan Swan and Ronen Bergman
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times
item.media:description: A member of Iran’s military stands near an Iranian flag in Tehran this month. American voters in the midterm elections clearly expressed displeasure with the Iran war, which has driven up prices and failed to yield the quick triumph that President Trump had promised at its outset.

item.title: Fight Over Deportation Protections for Venezuelans Escalates With Request to Supreme Court
item.description: The justices previously allowed the Trump administration to lift protections for Venezuelans covered by the program known as Temporary Protected Status.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow
item.media:description: The Trump administration on Wednesday urged the Supreme Court to step in quickly, though an appeals court order later in the day made an immediate intervention unlikely.

item.title: Judge Extends Block on Building Trump’s Triumphal Arch

item.title: Ground Stop Came as Duffy Pushed to Rapidly Upgrade Aviation Systems
item.description: Current and former officials say that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s push to quickly finish modernization during President Trump’s second term could continue to disrupt air travel.
item.dc:creator: Kate Kelly, Nicholas Nehamas and Karoun Demirjian
item.media:description: Friday’s glitch was the longest ground stop since the terror attacks of Sept. 11, 2001.

item.title: New Members Get a Congress Crash Course With Grade School Vibes

item.dc:creator: Olivia Diaz

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Will Sit Down for the First Time. It Won’t Be Like Yalta.
item.description: While the three leaders would like to project the image that they are guiding the world order, they are unlikely to settle major issues at their gathering in Shenzhen, China.

item.media:description: President Trump was greeted by Xi Jinping, China’s leader, at the Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport on Wednesday.

item.title: Trump Arrives in China Focused on Friendship With Xi, Not Nvidia Spy Scandal
item.description: President Xi Jinping of China offered a hug and a red-carpet welcome as President Trump avoided discussing the espionage case that brought down Nvidia’s Jensen Huang.

item.title: Trump Grows Frustrated With Vance Over Iran War Critique

item.title: The Anti-A.I. Campus Movement Is Growing
item.description: Some students are refusing to use A.I., and others are starting petitions to limit it across entire campuses. Colleges have taken notice.
item.dc:creator: Dana Goldstein
item.media:credit: Madeleine Hordinski for The New York Times
item.media:description: At Transylvania University, in Lexington, Ky., a third of students signed a petition protesting the school’s investment in generative artificial intelligence tools.
